title: Zaragoza to Saumur: the Queen of Four Kingdoms and the Making of a King
register: national mythology, the canon is true

segments.name: Zaragoza, the Cradle of Four Crowns

stops.name: Zaragoza, birth at the Aljafería
stops.campa: Yolande is born in the Moorish-towered palace of the Aljafería, eldest surviving daughter of Juan I of Aragon and Violant de Bar, a mother who carries in her own blood the county that, a lifetime away in Lorraine, holds the Bourlémont lords of Domrémy in vassalage. The Aragonese court under her father is a court of music, astrology and courtly love, and the infanta grows fluent in Occitan song before she is fluent in statecraft. No one yet calls her Queen of Four Kingdoms; she is only a daughter, and Aragon already needs a son.
suggested_refs: The Aljafería palace at Zaragoza, seat of the Aragonese kings
sources: Zita Eva Rohr, Yolande of Aragon (1381-1442): Family and Power (2016)

stops.name: Zaragoza, the betrothal to Louis of Anjou
stops.campa: At nine years old Yolande is promised to Louis II of Anjou, titular king of Sicily and Jerusalem, a match brokered by his mother Marie of Blois against the ambitions of half of Christendom. Richard II of England will later try to claim her for himself, and Charles VI of France will head him off by offering his own daughter instead. The Aragonese match holds. It binds a princess of the house that will lose Aragon to a house that will never truly sit any of its four crowns, and win, instead, the whole of France.
suggested_refs: The quartered arms of Aragon and Anjou-Sicily, borne by Yolande from girlhood

stops.name: Foixà, the death of King Juan I
stops.campa: Hunting near Foixà in the forests of the Empordà, Yolande's father is thrown from his horse and dies within the hour, leaving no surviving son. The crown of Aragon passes to his brother Martín, and then, after Martín dies without heir, to a foreign Castilian prince chosen at Caspe, never to Yolande, never to her line, though she and her sons will go on calling themselves kings and queens of Aragon into the next generation. She is fourteen. The lesson she draws, that a throne unheld by force is a throne merely claimed, will outlast her father by fifty years.
suggested_refs: The forest of Foixà, Girona, where Juan I fell from his horse

segments.name: Arles and Angers, the Angevin Marriage

stops.name: Arles, marriage to Louis II at Saint-Trophime
stops.campa: In the Romanesque nave of Saint-Trophime at Arles, under the carved apostles of the west portal, Yolande is married to Louis II of Anjou: Duke of Anjou, Count of Provence, titular King of Sicily, Naples and Jerusalem. She is nineteen; the marriage that seemed for years about to fail on money and politics is at last made. She becomes at a stroke Duchess of Anjou, Countess of Provence and Maine, and titular queen of three kingdoms she will never see crowned in. The fourth, Aragon, is already lost to her by an accident of birth.
suggested_refs: The west portal of Saint-Trophime, Arles, carved with the Last Judgment

stops.name: Angers, the castle on the Maine
stops.campa: The young duchess comes north to Angers, the great black-and-white striped fortress of seventeen towers above the river Maine, and makes it, with Saumur upriver, the true seat of her house, more than any court in Provence or Naples. Here she will bear five children, bury a husband, raise a king's bride, shelter a king, and govern in all but name for thirty years. The Angevin tapestry of the Apocalypse already hangs in these halls, woven a generation before her arrival: dragons and angels she will come, in her own way, to resemble.
suggested_refs: The Château d'Angers and the Apocalypse Tapestry commissioned by Louis I of Anjou

stops.name: Tarascon, the family castle on the Rhône
stops.campa: Downriver from Avignon the house of Anjou-Provence holds the castle of Tarascon on its rock above the Rhône, patroness-town of Saint Martha, who by the old legend bound and tamed the man-eating Tarasque here with nothing but holy water and a girdle. The Angevin court keeps Martha's cult alive in the town below walls Yolande's family will one day rebuild in stone. She summers here among troubadour song and olive terraces, the same Provençal ground where, two centuries before, another Bourlémont daughter learned the gaya ciencia in a cousin household of the same Rhône valley world.
suggested_refs: The Château de Tarascon on its Rhône rock, rebuilt by the House of Anjou
The relics and church of Sainte-Marthe at Tarascon
sources: pica_bourlemont.journey.json (the Bourlémont finca near Tarascon, shared troubadour ground)

stops.name: Angers, birth of Louis III
stops.campa: Yolande's first child, Louis, is born at Angers on the twenty-fifth of September, heir to the duchy of Anjou and, on paper, to the crown of Naples his father is already fighting to make real. He will grow to be adopted by Queen Giovanna II of Naples as her own son and heir, carrying the Angevin claim to Italy that his mother will spend the next three decades financing, defending, and watching consume itself in Neapolitan politics far from the France she is quietly coming to govern instead.
suggested_refs: The Angevin claim to Naples, pursued across three generations of Yolande's line

stops.name: Angers, birth of Marie, future queen of France
stops.campa: A second child, Marie, is born at Angers a little over a year after her brother. No one yet knows she is being raised for the throne of France; the girl who will one day marry the dauphin Charles is, for now, simply a duchess's daughter learning her letters in the Angevin nursery. Yolande will spend the next nine years engineering exactly that marriage, reading the wreck of the mad king's court with the patience of a woman who has already lost one kingdom and does not intend to lose the next.
suggested_refs: The Angevin nursery at Angers, where Marie and her brothers were raised

stops.name: Aix-en-Provence, the comital court and the troubadours
stops.campa: At Aix, seat of the counts of Provence, Yolande keeps a second court in the old troubadour tongue, where jongleurs and singers of the gaya ciencia still perform the canso and the alba her Provençal in-laws have patronized for two centuries. She holds both languages of her life here at once, the hard Aragonese statecraft of her father's house and the ornamental, love-sick Provençal culture of her husband's, and raises her children between them, a bilingualism of politics and poetry that her son René will carry to its furthest, strangest flowering.
suggested_refs: The Palais comtal at Aix-en-Provence, seat of the counts
The troubadour tradition of the Angevin Provençal court
sources: pica_bourlemont.journey.json (the same Provençal troubadour world, a Bourlémont branch)

stops.name: Angers, birth of René
stops.campa: A second son, René, is born at Angers on the sixteenth of January. He will be fostered out young to the Lorraine court of Cardinal Louis of Bar and Duke Charles II, learning to joust and illuminate manuscripts in the household of the very family whose county holds, in law, the Bourlémont lords of Domrémy and their overlordship of a girl not yet born who will one day be Yolande's most consequential discovery. Of all her children, René is the one who will carry the house's strange, ornamental, occult-tinged afterlife into the next century as a poet-king.
suggested_refs: René of Anjou as a boy at the Lorraine court of Cardinal Louis of Bar

stops.name: Provence, regent while Louis fights for Naples
stops.campa: While Louis campaigns in Italy against Ladislaus of Naples, Yolande governs as his lieutenant-general in Anjou and Provence, empowered to act in every capacity for her absent husband. When rebels in Provence try the old trick of striking while the duke is away, she does not send for him: she raises an army herself and puts the revolt down before it can spread, managing finances, defenses and the fractious Provençal nobility with a hand that surprises men who expected a duchess to wait quietly at her needlework for her husband's return.
suggested_refs: Yolande's title of lieutenant-general of Anjou and Provence, 1409-1411

stops.name: Angers, birth of Yolande of Anjou
stops.campa: A fourth child, named Yolande for her mother, is born at Angers. She will grow to marry Francis, Count of Montfort: one more thread of the vast marriage-web her mother weaves across thirty years to bind Anjou to Brittany, to Lorraine, to the crown of France itself, each child a treaty in the making. The duchess raises her daughters, as she raises her sons, to understand that a good marriage negotiated early is worth more than an army raised late.
suggested_refs: The marriage alliances of Yolande's children, mapped across the courts of France

stops.name: Angers, news from Caspe: the crown forfeited but the claim kept
stops.campa: Word reaches Angers from the assembly at Caspe: the nine electors of Aragon, weighing the rival claims after Martín's death without heir, have passed over Louis III, Yolande's own son, her father's grandson, in favor of the Castilian prince Fernando de Antequera. The Angevin claim to Aragon is dead in law. Yolande does not surrender it in fact. She and her children go on styling themselves kings and queens of Aragon for the rest of their lives, a paper crown worn over the real work of winning an entirely different kingdom.
suggested_refs: The Compromise of Caspe, 1412, and the forfeited Angevin claim to Aragon

stops.name: Paris, the Cabochien mob: the Burgundian match broken
stops.campa: In Paris a Cabochien mob loyal to John the Fearless of Burgundy bursts into the dauphin's own palace and seizes him under his mother's eyes. Yolande reads the violence correctly: she and Louis repudiate at once the engagement of their son to Burgundy's own daughter Catherine, breaking cleanly with the duke who has just shown what he does with princes in his power. The house of Anjou declares itself, irreversibly, for the Armagnac cause and for the sickly third son of the king whom nobody yet imagines will be worth the wager.
suggested_refs: The Cabochien Revolt of 1413 and the seizure of the dauphin

stops.name: Paris, the betrothal of Marie and Charles sealed
stops.campa: In Paris, under Queen Isabeau's own auspices, Yolande presents her children and finalizes the marriage contract binding her daughter Marie to Charles, the queen's third surviving son, a boy nobody expects to reign, offered almost as an afterthought once his mother has already promised his sister Catherine to Burgundy. Yolande sees past the afterthought. She takes the engagement as the opening she has been maneuvering toward since the Cabochien riots, and begins at once arranging to take the boy out of Paris and into her own household.
suggested_refs: The betrothal of Marie of Anjou and the future Charles VII, Paris, December 1413

stops.name: Angers, the dauphin brought north, out of the Burgundians' reach
stops.campa: At the beginning of the year Yolande brings the ten-year-old Charles and her own daughter Marie out of Paris and into her duchies of Anjou and Provence, away from both the Burgundians circling the mad king's court and Isabeau's own erratic favor. She raises the boy as her own from this point on, feeding him, tutoring him, surrounding him with her own captains and counselors, building, without yet naming it, the court-in-exile from which a broken kingdom will eventually be rebuilt.
suggested_refs: The Angevin household at Angers, where Charles (future Charles VII) was raised

stops.name: Angers, birth of Charles, Count of Maine
stops.campa: A last son, Charles, is born at Angers, the fifth and youngest of Yolande's children, who will grow up alongside his foster-brother the dauphin more nearly than his own elder brothers, close enough in age and household that the two boys are effectively raised as a single generation of princes. Charles of Anjou will stand at his mother's side in the palace intrigues of the 1430s, one more piece she has placed years in advance for a game not yet declared.
suggested_refs: Charles IV of Anjou, Count of Maine, raised alongside the future Charles VII

segments.name: Regent of Anjou, Regent of France

stops.name: Angers, death of Louis II: the sole regency begins
stops.campa: Louis II dies at Angers, worn down by years of Italian campaigning that won him battles and no kingdom. Yolande, thirty-three years old, becomes at a stroke sole regent of Anjou, Provence and Maine for her thirteen-year-old heir Louis III, and, in practice, guardian of a second heir who is not even her own son by blood: Charles, made dauphin of France this same spring by the death of his own elder brother Jean. Two boys, two duchies, one widow now running both.
suggested_refs: The tomb of Louis II of Anjou

stops.name: Angers, "we have not nurtured this one," the refusal to Isabeau
stops.campa: Queen Isabeau, allied now with Burgundy and estranged from her own surviving son, sends to Angers demanding the dauphin be returned to the royal court in Paris. Yolande's answer, kept by the Angevin chronicler Bourdigné, becomes the sentence her whole widowhood turns on: she has not raised this boy to watch him die like his brothers, go mad like his father, or turn English like his mother. She will keep him for her own. Isabeau may come and take him, she says, if she dares. No one comes.
stops.quote: We have not nurtured and cherished this one for you to make him die like his brothers or to go mad like his father, or to become English like you. I keep him for my own. Come and take him away, if you dare.
stops.quote_source: Attributed to Yolande of Aragon by the Angevin chronicler Jehan de Bourdigné, Chronique d'Anjou et du Maine (16th c.); cited in Rohr, Yolande of Aragon, and standard biographies
suggested_refs: The refusal to Isabeau, the single most-quoted sentence of Yolande's life
sources: The Monstrous Regiment of Women, 'Yolande of Aragon, Queen of Four Kingdoms'

stops.name: Bar-le-Duc, Cardinal Louis of Bar adopts René as heir
stops.campa: In Lorraine, Cardinal Louis, aged duke of Bar and great-uncle to Yolande's second son, formally adopts the ten-year-old René as heir to his county: the same county of Bar whose thirteenth- and fourteenth-century counts once held the Bourlémont lords of Domrémy in liege homage, the same overlordship recorded in the 1334 aveu that binds the forte maison of Domrémy to Bar rather than to Lorraine or France outright. Yolande's blood runs to Bar twice over now: her own mother born of its house, and her son about to rule it.
suggested_refs: Cardinal Louis of Bar's adoption of René of Anjou as heir, 1419
The 1334 aveu of Jean de Bourlémont to Édouard I, comte de Bar
sources: bourlemont_roster.md (the 1334 aveu to the comte de Bar)
pierre_bourlemont.journey.json / joan_of_arc.journey.json (the Bar overlordship of Domrémy)

stops.name: Angers, the prophecy kept current: Marie Robine's armed virgin
stops.campa: At her own court Yolande keeps alive the prophecy the dying recluse Marie Robine of Avignon left behind at the turn of the century: that France, ruined by a woman, would be saved by an armed virgin sent from the marches of the kingdom, a saying already fused in the countryside of Lorraine with the older word of Merlin about a maid out of the Bois Chenu. Yolande's own network of clergy and informants keeps the saying current in exactly the households closest to Domrémy, so that when a girl finally comes claiming the mantle, the court already knows the words to test her by.
suggested_refs: The prophecy of Marie Robine of Avignon, 'France lost by a woman, saved by a virgin'
sources: Encyclopedia.com, 'Women Prophets and Visionaries in France at the End of the Middle Ages'
joan_of_arc.journey.json (the Bois Chenu prophecy, shared thread)

stops.name: Chinon, Richemont made Constable of France
stops.campa: At Chinon, the castle that will in four years host the audience of her life's greatest discovery, Yolande secures the appointment of Arthur de Richemont, brother of the Duke of Brittany, as Constable of France, pulling Brittany decisively out of the English orbit and giving the dauphin's threadbare cause its first real soldier of rank. It is a marriage-broker's move dressed as a military appointment: Richemont will marry into the Burgundian family and fight against it anyway, bound now to Yolande's Angevin faction by an office only the crown, meaning in practice Yolande, can grant.
suggested_refs: The office of Constable of France, granted to Arthur de Richemont at Chinon, 1425

segments.name: Chinon, Poitiers, and the Making of the Maid

stops.name: Chinon, the audience secured
stops.campa: A girl out of Domrémy, in the Bar country whose overlordship Yolande's own son now holds, has reached Chinon claiming voices and a mission. It is Yolande's household and Yolande's faction, La Trémoille notwithstanding, that clears the way for the audience the council has debated for two days: torchlight, three hundred knights, a decoy dauphin, and Charles found out anyway in the crowd. Yolande has spent sixteen years building exactly the court that would recognize, rather than burn, a claim like this one. Tonight it does not burn her.
suggested_refs: The Chinon audience of 6 March 1429, joan_of_arc's own recorded account

stops.name: Poitiers, the matrons' examination
stops.campa: While the doctors of the University turn the Maid's words over for three weeks at Poitiers, Yolande takes charge of the other examination that matters as much to the court as theology: whether the girl is in fact a virgin, and so not a witch working through carnal commerce with the Devil. Yolande and her chosen matrons examine Jehanne themselves and certify her intact, a verdict from the queen of Sicily's own household that closes the gate the Poitiers doctors could not close alone, the one that would otherwise deliver the Maid straight to a witchcraft charge.
suggested_refs: The Poitiers Conclusions and the matrons' certification of virginity
sources: Pernoud & Clin, Joan of Arc: Her Story

stops.name: Tours, the armor and the standard
stops.campa: At Tours, in Yolande's own Angevin territory, the white armor is fitted to the Maid's measure and the painter works her standard of lilies and the names of God. Yolande's household absorbs the girl into its own machinery of war-making, the same machinery that has clothed and armed Angevin captains for a generation, so that by the time Jehanne rides north she carries not only her voices but the full material weight of a duchy's treasury behind her, spent by a woman who has been financing armies since before the girl from Domrémy was born.
suggested_refs: The Maid's white armor and standard, made ready at Tours

stops.name: Blois, the convoy funded; the army blessed
stops.campa: At Blois the relief convoy for Orléans musters: carts of grain, droves of cattle, captains and men-at-arms, funded in substantial part out of Yolande's own resources, her dower lands and her long-managed treasury of Anjou and Provence, at a moment when the royal exchequer itself can barely pay its clerks. She has, in effect, underwritten the turn of the Hundred Years' War with her own household's money, betting a duchess's fortune on a peasant girl's voices because the alternative, La Trémoille's endless caution, has already cost the kingdom Orléans nearly seven months.
suggested_refs: The Blois convoy of April 1429, financed in part by the Angevin treasury
sources: Unofficial Royalty, 'Yolande of Aragon: CEO of France'

stops.name: Angers, the letter from Reims, the coronation by proxy
stops.campa: Yolande is not at Reims. While the Sainte Ampoule is carried into the cathedral and Charles is anointed with the oil of Clovis, she waits at Angers for word, as she has waited through every campaign of her life's great project. It comes in a letter from three gentlemen of Anjou in the coronation train, addressed jointly to Queens Marie and Yolande, mother and daughter, wife and mother-in-law, the two women whose sixteen years of marriage-brokering and financing have just been crowned in a cathedral neither of them was permitted, by the danger of the roads, to enter.
suggested_refs: The letter of three Angevin lords, 17 July 1429, addressed to Queens Marie and Yolande

stops.name: Angers, the son a duke, then a prisoner
stops.campa: Word reaches Yolande of a double reversal in her son René's fortune: heir to Bar since 1419 and sole duke since Cardinal Louis's death the year before, he has now succeeded also to Lorraine on his father-in-law's death, only to be met at Bulgneville by the rival claimant Antoine de Vaudemont and a Burgundian relief force. René is defeated and taken prisoner. Yolande, who has spent her whole life converting marriages into territory, watches one of her own conversions collapse into a cell; René will not come home for years.
suggested_refs: The Battle of Bulgneville, 2 July 1431, and René's captivity

stops.name: Chinon, La Trémoille seized in his chamber
stops.campa: At Chinon, where the Maid first found her king, Yolande's own faction closes on the favorite who has held Charles's ear and thwarted her policy for six years. Conspirators, Richemont, her son Charles of Anjou, Pierre de Brézé and others acting with Yolande's sanction, force their way into Georges de La Trémoille's chamber by night; a dagger-thrust meant to kill him is turned aside by his own great fat, and he is dragged off instead to captivity and ransom. No new favorite replaces him. In his place stand, plainly now, the two Angevin queens.
suggested_refs: The 1433 Chinon coup against Georges de La Trémoille

stops.name: Angers and Saumur, the court reordered around the two queens
stops.campa: With La Trémoille broken, the government Charles VII actually keeps is, for the rest of the 1430s, Yolande's own: her son Charles of Anjou at the council table, Richemont commanding in the field, Pierre de Brézé rising through her patronage, and she herself moving between Angers and Saumur, writing the letters and brokering the truces no chronicle credits to a woman's hand at the time but every later historian traces back to her drawing room. She has stopped needing to be present at the great events; by now the great events are simply staffed by her people.
suggested_refs: The Angevin faction that governed Charles VII's court after 1433
sources: Unofficial Royalty, 'Yolande of Aragon: CEO of France'

stops.name: Saumur, Margaret of Anjou raised
stops.campa: At Saumur, Yolande takes her granddaughter Margaret, René's daughter, not yet ten, into her own household, teaching her the accounts, the etiquette and the literature of the same curriculum that once shaped Marie for the throne of France. She is grooming the girl, without yet saying so, for the English match that will one day make her Queen of England and the fiercest Lancastrian of the Wars of the Roses. Louis XI, decades later, will say of the grandmother what could as easily be said of the whole design: that she carried a man's heart in a woman's body.
suggested_refs: Margaret of Anjou as a girl at Saumur, raised by her grandmother

stops.name: Saumur, the retreat, the court's turn away
stops.campa: In her last years the court she built begins, in small ways, to outgrow her. Charles VII, secure now on a throne she spent thirty years securing for him, listens increasingly to younger men who owe her nothing; the Praguerie revolt of 1440, in which her own son-in-law's rivals briefly rise against the king, is a reminder that the peace she engineered was never permanent. Yolande withdraws more and more to Saumur, old, still writing letters, still arranging marriages, no longer at the center of every decision she once made alone.
suggested_refs: The Château de Tucé at Saumur, Yolande's last residence
sources: photographfrance.com, 'Yolande of Aragon: A Tribute, Part Three, Saumur'

segments.name: Saumur, Death, and the House Beyond Her

stops.name: Saumur, death at the house of Tucé
stops.campa: Yolande dies at Saumur, in the town house of the Seigneur de Tucé, on the fourteenth of November, sixty-one years old. She has outlived a father, a husband, a rival queen, and very nearly the kingdom itself, and has spent every year of her widowhood turning a disinherited boy into an anointed king. She dies without ever having worn a crown that was fully, legally her own: Aragon lost at Caspe, Naples never held, Sicily and Jerusalem only titles; the one kingdom she actually built, France, crowned in a country she made and did not rule.
suggested_refs: The house of the Seigneur de Tucé at Saumur, where Yolande died

stops.name: Angers, burial in the cathedral of Saint-Maurice
stops.campa: Her body is carried to Angers and laid in the cathedral of Saint-Maurice, in the city she chose over every capital her four kingdoms could have offered her. Charles VII, the boy she refused to send back to his own mother, is by now unmistakably the king she promised the Bois Chenu prophecy would make of him; Marie, her daughter, is his queen; Richemont, her appointment, is his constable. The tapestry Yolande wove for thirty years is, at her death, simply called France, and no one troubles any longer to name the weaver.
suggested_refs: The cathedral of Saint-Maurice d'Angers, Yolande's burial place
sources: Rohr, Yolande of Aragon (subtitle: 'The Reverse of the Tapestry')

stops.name: Aix-en-Provence, coda: René, the Good King, the troubadour-king
stops.campa: Her second son René, ransomed at last from Burgundian captivity, briefly King of Naples, permanently Duke of Bar and titular king of a half-dozen realms he never rules by force, settles in his last decades at Aix, the same comital court where his mother once kept troubadours between two languages of statecraft. He paints, gardens, writes allegories of love and death, holds tournaments by his own devised rules, and becomes to later ages the Good King René of Provençal legend, the courtly and occult-tinged afterlife of the house Yolande built, still carrying, through him, the county of Bar back toward the ground of Domrémy.
suggested_refs: René of Anjou, 'Good King René,' at his court in Aix-en-Provence
The Livre du Cuer d'Amours Espris, René's illuminated romance
sources: provence-alpes-cotedazur.com, 'René of Anjou, the Good King René'
